propositions: Rename the transition command's --force-close flag to --force for consistency with rebar claim's spelling and consolidate two distinct force flags into one
The new --force[=<reason>] flag bypasses whichever gate the transition would hit, dispatched by target status: start-work gate on open->in_progress, completion gate on ->closed
--force-close is rejected explicitly with a CommandError naming --force rather than silently skipped by the token loop, to prevent silent failures when stale callers use the retired spelling
A bare --force on close yields reason '(no reason given)'; --force=<reason> becomes the audit note, and --force --reason=x on start-work preserves x as the note
The rename must be completed tree-wide across code, docs, and tests in a single change with no compatibility alias, following the clean-break operator decision

Post-merge defects in concurrent changes (dependency_audit.py, canary_bridge.py) require the parser rejection branch to catch stale flag usage at runtime and a regression test to validate generated argv against the real parser
